page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. This instance does not include local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also demonstrate average performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a balanced compute-to-memory density for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of bundled local storage. The hardware is suited for workloads that benefit from parallel processing but do not require high single-thread performance. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded web serving, database operations, and general-purpose parallel computing tasks.
